subject: science
name: Science and Technology
exam: SEE, 2 hr 30 min, FM 75 written (+25 internal/practical) | Biology, Physics, Chemistry, Astronomy and ICT

units.title: Scientific Learning
summary: Science is the organised study of nature through observation and experiment; technology applies scientific knowledge to solve problems.
The scientific method: problem → observation → hypothesis → experiment → data analysis → conclusion → report.
In an experiment there is one independent variable, a dependent variable that we measure, and controlled variables kept constant; a control group is used for comparison.
Accuracy is closeness to the true value; precision is closeness of repeated readings. Taking the mean of several readings reduces random error.
SI base units: metre (m), kilogram (kg), second (s), kelvin (K), ampere (A), candela (cd), mole (mol). Going to a smaller unit, multiply; to a bigger unit, divide.
Least count of a vernier = 1 MSD − 1 VSD (usually 0.01 cm); of a screw gauge = pitch / number of circular divisions (usually 0.01 mm).
Density = mass / volume; km/h to m/s: multiply by 5/18.
A project follows these steps: topic, plan, data collection, analysis, conclusion, report. A report has an introduction, methods, analysis, conclusion and references.

units.title: Classification of Living Beings
topics: characteristics of Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia

sections.title: Characteristics of Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia

summary: Taxonomy is the identification, naming and classification of organisms. Linnaeus is the father of taxonomy; Whittaker proposed five kingdoms in 1969.
The hierarchy is Kingdom → Phylum → Class → Order → Family → Genus → Species; the species is the basic unit.
Binomial nomenclature: two Latin names, genus (capital) then species (small letter), in italics or underlined.
Monera: prokaryotic, unicellular (bacteria, cyanobacteria); binary fission.
Protista: unicellular eukaryotes (Amoeba, Paramecium, Euglena).
Fungi: chitin cell wall, hyphae, saprophytic or parasitic, spores (yeast, mushroom).
Plantae: multicellular, cellulose wall, photosynthesis; algae, bryophytes, pteridophytes, gymnosperms, angiosperms.
Animalia: multicellular, heterotrophic, no cell wall; invertebrate phyla and five classes of vertebrates (fish, amphibians, reptiles, birds, mammals).

units.title: Honey Bee
summary: Honey bees belong to genus Apis, class Insecta, order Hymenoptera. Wild species: A. dorsata, A. laboriosa, A. florea; domesticated: A. cerana, A. mellifera.
The colony has three castes: one queen (fertile female), thousands of workers (sterile females) and drones (males).
Life cycle: egg → larva → pupa → adult (complete metamorphosis). Egg-to-adult time: queen 16 days, worker 21 days, drone 24 days.
Fertilised eggs give queens and workers (diet decides which); unfertilised eggs give drones (parthenogenesis).
Division of labour among workers by age: cleaner, nurse, house bee (comb builder), guard, forager. Bees communicate by round and waggle dances.
The comb is made of hexagonal wax cells; the brood is at the centre, pollen around it and honey above.
Bee-keeping tools: movable-frame hive, queen excluder, smoker, veil, hive tool, honey extractor.
Products: honey, beeswax, royal jelly, propolis, pollen and bee venom. Bees also pollinate crops.

units.title: Heredity
summary: Heredity is the passing of characters from parents to offspring through genes. Mendel, the father of genetics, worked with pea plants and discovered the laws of inheritance.
Monohybrid cross Tt × Tt gives phenotypic ratio 3 : 1 and genotypic ratio 1 : 2 : 1; a test cross with the recessive parent shows whether a dominant plant is pure.
Dihybrid cross RrYy × RrYy gives 9 : 3 : 3 : 1.
Laws: dominance, segregation (purity of gametes), independent assortment.
Cell → nucleus → chromosome → DNA → gene. Humans have 46 chromosomes (22 pairs autosomes + XX or XY). DNA is a double helix with A–T and C–G pairing.
Sex is decided by the father's sperm: X-sperm gives a girl, Y-sperm gives a boy; chance 50 : 50.
Sex-linked recessive disorders (colour blindness, haemophilia) are commoner in males.
Chromosomal disorders: Down's (47, trisomy 21), Turner's (XO, 45), Klinefelter's (XXY, 47). Genetic counselling helps prevention.

units.title: Physiological Structure and Life Process
summary: The CNS (brain + spinal cord) and the PNS (nerves) coordinate quickly using electrical impulses; the endocrine glands coordinate slowly using hormones.
Neuron: dendrites, cell body, axon, myelin sheath. Reflex arc: receptor → sensory neuron → spinal cord → motor neuron → effector.
Brain: cerebrum (thinking), cerebellum (balance), medulla (involuntary actions). Pituitary is the master gland; thyroxine needs iodine; insulin controls blood sugar.
Human reproduction: sperm and egg meet in the fallopian tube; the zygote implants in the uterus; gestation about 280 days. Menstrual cycle 28 days, ovulation about day 14.
Blood = plasma + RBC (oxygen) + WBC (defence) + platelets (clotting). Blood groups A, B, AB, O.
Heart has four chambers; double circulation (pulmonary and systemic). Cardiac output = heart rate × stroke volume; normal BP 120/80 mm Hg.
Nephron: filtration (glomerulus), reabsorption (tubule), secretion; about 180 L filtered and 1.5 L urine per day. Dialysis treats kidney failure.
Homeostasis: constant internal conditions by negative feedback: body temperature 37 °C (hypothalamus), blood glucose (insulin and glucagon), water (ADH).

units.title: Nature and Environment
summary: An ecosystem is the living (producers, consumers, decomposers) and non-living parts of a place interacting. Energy flows in one direction (10% passes to the next level); matter is recycled in carbon, nitrogen and water cycles.
Food chains join to form a food web: producer → herbivore → carnivore → top carnivore.

Air pollutants: CO, CO₂, SO₂, NOₓ, particles, CFCs; water pollution from sewage, chemicals and fertilisers (eutrophication); soil pollution from plastic and agrochemicals; noise above 85 dB harms hearing.

Greenhouse gases (CO₂, CH₄, N₂O, CFCs) trap heat. Global warming melts glaciers, raises sea level and changes rainfall. CFCs thin the ozone layer, allowing more UV rays; the Montreal Protocol controls them.
Waste is biodegradable or non-biodegradable. Follow the 3 Rs (reduce, reuse, recycle) and segregate at source; compost, biogas and sanitary landfill are the main treatments.
Conservation is wise use of resources: in-situ (parks, reserves, community forests) and ex-situ (zoos, gene banks). Nepal protects about 23% of its land; Chitwan was the first national park (1973).

units.title: Motion and Force
summary: Force is a push or a pull; unit newton. Net force zero means the forces are balanced.
Newton's first law: a body keeps its state of rest or uniform motion unless an unbalanced force acts. Inertia depends on mass.
Newton's second law: F = ma; also F = dfracΔ pt. 1 N gives 1 kg an acceleration of 1 m s⁻².
Newton's third law: action and reaction are equal and opposite and act on different bodies.
Momentum p = mv (kg m s⁻¹); impulse Ft = mv - mu. Without external force, m1u1 + m2u2 = m1v1 + m2v2.
Gravitation: F = Gdfracm1 m2d^2 with G = 6.67×10^-11 N m² kg⁻²; g = dfracGMR^2 = 9.8 m s⁻²; g is greatest at the poles and zero at the Earth's centre.
Weight W = mg (newton) changes from place to place; mass (kg) does not.
Free fall: v = gt, h = tfrac12 gt^2, v^2 = 2gh; for upward throw H = dfracu^22g, time of flight dfrac2ug.

units.title: Pressure
topics: Pressure in solids, liquids and gases

sections.title: Pressure in solids, liquids and gases

summary: Pressure = thrust ÷ area: P = F/A; unit pascal (1 Pa = 1 N m⁻²). Small area gives high pressure.
Liquid pressure: P = hρ g; it increases with depth and acts equally in all directions at a point.
Pascal's law: pressure on an enclosed fluid is transmitted equally in all directions. Hydraulic machine: F = f (A/a).
Atmospheric pressure at sea level = 76 cm Hg = 1.013×10^5 Pa; it decreases with altitude. A barometer measures it.
Archimedes' principle: upthrust = weight of fluid displaced = Vρ g; apparent weight = weight − upthrust.
A body sinks if ρb > ρl, floats if ρb < ρl; for a floating body, upthrust = weight.
Ships float because their average density is less than water's; submarines, hydrometers and balloons use the same law.

units.title: Heat
summary: Heat is energy (joule); temperature tells hotness. Heat flows from higher to lower temperature. T(K) = t(°C) + 273.
Linear expansion: Δ L = α L0 Δ T. Bimetallic strips, rail gaps and tyre-fitting use expansion.
Water contracts from 0 °C to 4 °C and has maximum density at 4 °C; this saves aquatic life in frozen lakes.
Specific heat capacity c: heat to raise 1 kg by 1 °C; Q = mcΔ T (water c = 4200 J kg⁻¹ °C⁻¹). Heat lost = heat gained in mixing.
Latent heat: Q = mL with no change in temperature. Lf(ice) = 3.36×10^5 J kg⁻¹, Lv(water) = 2.26×10^6 J kg⁻¹.
Conduction (solids, particles vibrate), convection (fluids, particles move), radiation (waves, no medium needed).
Dull black surfaces absorb and emit heat well; shiny surfaces reflect heat. A thermos flask reduces all three modes.

units.title: Wave
summary: A wave transfers energy without transferring matter. Transverse: vibration ⟂ wave direction; longitudinal: vibration ∥ wave direction. v = fλ, T = 1/f.
Sound is a longitudinal mechanical wave; cannot travel in a vacuum; fastest in solids. Audible range 20 Hz–20 kHz. Echo needs at least 17 m: d = vt/2.
Loudness depends on amplitude, pitch on frequency, quality on waveform.
Reflection: ∠ i = ∠ r. Mirror formula dfrac1f = dfrac1u + dfrac1v, f = R/2, m = v/u.
Refraction: dfracsin isin r = n = dfraccv; total internal reflection when light goes dense → rare with i > C, where sin C = 1/n.
Lens formula dfrac1f = dfrac1u + dfrac1v; power P = 1/f (m) in dioptre; convex is positive, concave is negative.
Myopia is corrected by a concave lens, hypermetropia by a convex lens. Compound microscope and telescope use two convex lenses.

units.title: Electricity and Magnetism
summary: I = Q/t (A); V = work per unit charge (V). Ohm's law: V = IR at constant temperature.
R = ρ l/A. Series: Rs = R1 + R2 + cdots; parallel: dfrac1Rp = dfrac1R1 + dfrac1R2 + cdots.
Power P = VI = I^2R = V^2/R; energy W = Pt; 1 kWh = 3.6×10⁶ J. Heat H = I^2Rt. A fuse breaks an overloaded circuit.
A current produces a magnetic field (Oersted). Right-hand grip rule gives its direction; a solenoid with an iron core is an electromagnet.
A conductor carrying current in a magnetic field feels a force (Fleming's left-hand rule). The DC motor uses it and a split-ring commutator.
Electromagnetic induction: changing flux induces an emf (Faraday); its direction opposes the change (Lenz). Fleming's right-hand rule gives the direction.
AC generator: mechanical → electrical energy, slip rings, output AC (50 Hz in Nepal).
Transformer (AC only): dfracVsVp = dfracNsNp and VpIp = VsIs for an ideal one; high-voltage transmission reduces I^2R loss.

units.title: Universe
summary: The universe is everything. 1 light year = 9.46×10^12 km (distance); 1 AU = 1.5×10^8 km. Sunlight takes 8 min 20 s to reach the Earth.

A star is a ball of hot gas shining by nuclear fusion of hydrogen. Life cycle: nebula → protostar → main sequence → red giant → white dwarf (Sun-like) or supernova → neutron star / black hole (massive).
A galaxy is a system of billions of stars. The Milky Way is a spiral galaxy. Constellations are patterns of stars; the Pole Star shows north.
The solar system has eight planets: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars (terrestrial), Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune (giants), plus dwarf planets, asteroids, comets and meteors. T^2 = r^3 (years, AU).
Big Bang: the universe began about 13.8 billion years ago and is still expanding. Evidence: red shift of galaxies, cosmic microwave background, abundance of H and He.
Satellites stay in orbit because gravity supplies the circular-motion force. Geostationary satellites orbit at 36,000 km with a 24 h period.
Milestones: Sputnik 1 (1957), Gagarin (1961), Apollo 11 (1969), Hubble (1990), ISS (1998), NepaliSat-1 (2019).

units.title: Information and Communication Technology
summary: A computer takes input, processes data using the CPU (ALU + CU) and memory, and gives output. Hardware is physical; software is programs (system, utility, application).
RAM is volatile; ROM is permanent. 1 byte = 8 bits; 1 KB = 1024 B; 1 MB = 1024 KB; 1 GB = 1024 MB. Computers use the binary system.
A network connects computers: LAN, MAN, WAN; topologies include star, bus and ring.
The internet is a network of networks; the WWW is a service on it. Important terms: ISP, IP address, URL, browser, search engine, e-mail, bandwidth.
Safe use: antivirus, firewall, strong passwords; beware of phishing, hacking and viruses.
E-commerce is buying and selling online (B2C, B2B, C2C, G2C), with digital payment; it saves time and widens choice but carries risks of fraud.
ICT is used in education, health, banking, governance, agriculture, transport and many other fields; emerging technologies are AI and IoT.
Cyber ethics requires respect for others, privacy and copyright. Cyber crime is punished by cyber law; in Nepal, the Electronic Transactions Act 2063 B.S.

units.title: Classification of Elements
summary: Dobereiner (triads), Newlands (octaves) and Mendeleev (periodic law by atomic mass) were early attempts; Moseley's modern periodic law uses atomic number.
The modern table has 18 groups and 7 periods; blocks are s, p, d and f.
Period number = number of shells; group number (1, 2) = valence electrons; groups 13 to 18: valence electrons + 10.
Valency = valence electrons (1 to 3) or 8 − valence electrons (4 to 7); noble gases are 0.
Down a group: atomic size increases; ionisation energy and electronegativity decrease; metallic character increases.
Across a period: atomic size decreases; ionisation energy and electronegativity increase; non-metallic character increases.
Group 1 = alkali metals, group 2 = alkaline earth metals, group 17 = halogens, group 18 = noble gases.

units.title: Chemical Reaction
summary: A chemical reaction forms new substances; it is shown by a balanced equation (reactants → products).
Types: combination, decomposition, displacement, double displacement, exothermic/endothermic and redox.
Mass is conserved: balance equations by writing coefficients, never by changing subscripts.
Rate of reaction increases with concentration, surface area, temperature and a catalyst.
Acids give H⁺, bases (alkalis) give OH⁻; pH below 7 is acidic, 7 is neutral, above 7 is basic.
Acid + base → salt + water is neutralisation; Acid + metal → salt + H₂; Acid + carbonate → salt + water + CO₂.
Important salts: NaCl, NaHCO₃, Na₂CO₃·10H₂O, plaster of Paris, bleaching powder.

units.title: Gases
topics: preparation of hydrogen, oxygen, carbon dioxide

sections.title: Preparation of hydrogen, oxygen and carbon dioxide

summary: Gas particles are far apart and move fast; gases have no fixed shape or volume, are compressible and exert pressure.
Temperature in gas laws must be in kelvin: T = t + 273.
Boyle's law (constant T): P1V1 = P2V2.
Charles' law (constant P): V1/T1 = V2/T2.
Combined: dfracP1V1T1 = dfracP2V2T2; STP is 273 K and 760 mm Hg.
H₂: Zn + dil. H₂SO₄; pop test. O₂: KClO₃ + MnO₂ heated; glowing splinter relights. CO₂: CaCO₃ + dil. HCl; lime water turns milky.
Uses: H₂ as fuel and in ammonia; O₂ in respiration and welding; CO₂ in fire extinguishers and soft drinks.

units.title: Metal and Non-metals
summary: Metals are lustrous, malleable, ductile and conduct heat and electricity; non-metals are dull, brittle and poor conductors (graphite and diamond are exceptions).
Metal oxides are basic; non-metal oxides are acidic; Al₂O₃ and ZnO are amphoteric.
Reactivity series: K, Na, Ca, Mg, Al, Zn, Fe, Pb, H, Cu, Hg, Ag, Au. A more reactive metal displaces a less reactive one; only metals above H liberate H₂ from dilute acids.
Ores of Fe: haematite and magnetite; Al: bauxite; Cu: copper pyrite.
Steps: crushing, concentration, calcination/roasting, reduction, refining. Reactive metals are extracted by electrolysis; middle metals by carbon reduction.
Iron is made in a blast furnace from haematite, coke and limestone; Al is extracted by electrolysis of alumina in cryolite.
Rusting needs oxygen and water; prevent it by painting, galvanising, plating and alloying.

units.title: Hydrocarbon and its Compounds
summary: Carbon is tetravalent and shows catenation; hydrocarbons contain only C and H.
Alkanes CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ (single bonds, substitution); alkenes CₙH₂ₙ (C=C, addition and polymerisation); alkynes CₙH₂ₙ₋₂ (C≡C, addition).
Unsaturated hydrocarbons decolourise bromine water and Baeyer's reagent; alkanes do not.
A homologous series has the same functional group and general formula, and members differ by –CH₂– (14 u).
Alcohols CₙH₂ₙ₊₁OH (–OH): ethanol is made by fermentation of sugar; it reacts with Na to give H₂; oxidises to ethanoic acid; methanol is poisonous.
Carboxylic acids CₙH₂ₙ₊₁COOH (–COOH): ethanoic acid (vinegar) is a weak acid, gives CO₂ with NaHCO₃, and forms esters with alcohols.

units.title: Chemicals used in Daily Life
summary: Soap is the sodium or potassium salt of a fatty acid, made by saponification of oil or fat with alkali; glycerol is a by-product. It cleans by forming micelles around grease.
Soap forms scum with hard water; detergents (synthetic) do not, but non-biodegradable ones pollute water.
Fertilisers supply N, P and K. Urea has 46 % N. Excess use causes soil damage and eutrophication.
Cement is made by heating limestone and clay at 1400 to 1500 °C and grinding the clinker with 2 to 3 % gypsum; mortar, concrete and RCC are its main products.
Glass is an amorphous solid made by fusing sand (SiO₂), soda ash (Na₂CO₃) and limestone (CaCO₃) at about 1500 °C; it is annealed by slow cooling.
Polymers are formed from monomers; thermoplastics soften on heating, thermosetting plastics do not.
Plastics are non-biodegradable, so reduce, reuse, recycle and refuse.
